items.title: [PD] Add L2-Only decode-side radix cache for disaggregated HiCache
items.body:
## Motivation

With hierarchical cache on the decode side of a PD-disaggregated deployment, inbound KV lands in HBM and every session's prefix stays resident there for reuse. At long context the working set dwarfs the device pool: 131K context across 64 sessions is 8.38M tokens against a `max_total_tokens` of 712K, i.e. 1175%, while the pool can only hold 5.45 full-length requests.

The device pool then pins at `token usage` 0.98, the decode scheduler degrades to a single running request, the preallocation backlog reaches 20, and admission back-pressures prefill.

This adds `--disaggregation-decode-l2-only-radix-cache`, which keeps the decode-side prefix cache in host memory and stages inbound KV there, so HBM holds only what in-flight requests actively need. At the same operating point the device pool sits at 0.31 with an empty preallocation backlog.

## Modifications

| area | change |
|---|---|
| `server_args.py`, `arg_groups/kv_cache_hook.py`, `arg_groups/pd_disaggregation_hook.py` | the new flag plus validation: decode side only, requires `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`, `--enable-hierarchical-cache` and `--hicache-mem-layout layer_first` |
| `disaggregation/decode.py` | host staging allocation at admission, per-tick MIN-alignment of the rank-local admission inputs, symmetric shortfall back-off |
| `disaggregation/decode_hicache_mixin.py` | the restore pipeline (Phase A advances in-flight DMAs, Phase B queues new `load_back` ops), per-tick device headroom accounting, host prefix pinning |
| `mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py` | `is_load_back_event_done_pure`, a pure-query variant of the existing `is_load_back_event_done`; skip the `-1` ack sentinel in `loading_check` |
| `mem_cache/pool_host/{group,mha}.py` | logical page size and group accessors used by staging |
| `managers/scheduler.py` | idle detection also waits for pending staging frees |
| `environ.py` | `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_UNIFORM_HICACHE_POLLING` makes the restore loop's load-back completion check rank-uniform by hoisting `loading_check()` to once per tick; `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_UNIFORM_HICACHE_FAILURE` takes the cross-rank union of restore failures. Both default off, L2-Only forces them on |

The rank-local admission inputs — host availability, request-pool and metadata free counts, restore readiness — are MIN-aligned once per tick through the existing `BasePrefixCache._all_reduce_attn_groups` helper, with multi-scalar cases packed into one tensor as `drain_storage_control_queues` and `check_hicache_events` already do. All new collective call sites are gated behind the new flag or behind SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_UNIFORM_HICACHE_FAILURE (default off), so with both off the path issues no additional collectives.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K and MMLU, flag off (B, hierarchical cache) against flag on (C, L2-Only), two passes each at `page_size` 1 / 16 / 64. All cells `exit=0`.

GSM8K accuracy:

| | ps=1 pass1 | ps=1 pass2 | ps=16 pass1 | ps=16 pass2 | ps=64 pass1 | ps=64 pass2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B (flag off) | 0.335 | 0.335 | 0.330 | 0.345 | 0.350 | 0.350 |
| C (flag on) | 0.335 | 0.335 | 0.330 | 0.345 | 0.350 | 0.350 |

Identical at all six points. MMLU accuracy falls in 0.539–0.547 across all 12 runs of both modes.

Three-round L3 test (write to storage, then serve purely from storage, then all three tiers coexisting): GSM8K 0.335 / 0.335 / 0.335, so the host-to-storage round trip does not perturb outputs.

A 41-cell acceptance matrix also passes in full (`PASS=41 FAIL=0`), covering non-page-aligned tails at `page_size` 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, a `--mem-fraction-static` sweep from 0.85 down to 0.65, host-pool exhaustion at 2 GB and 4 GB pools, and a 512-request long run. Each cell asserts server start, bench `exit=0`, a live `Decode batch` heartbeat within 90 s, and no `Traceback` / `KeyError` / CUDA error in the logs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3-32B, TP=2 prefill + TP=2 decode, mooncake, 131K context, hierarchical cache on, 64 clients with 32 in flight, 192 requests per cell, `page_size` 64. Both cells `exit=0`.

| metric | baseline | L2-Only | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| wall clock | 2h08m44s | 40m54s | **3.15x** |
| p99 TTFT | 583.70 | 279.13 | **2.09x** |
| avg TTFT per completed request | 335.6 (41 completed) | 159.3 (18 completed) | **2.11x** |
| output tok/s | 0.36 | 0.54 | **1.50x** |
| prefill tok/s | 238 | 1481 | **6.22x** |
| `token usage` peak | 0.98 | **0.31** | — |
| TPOT / ITL | 0.0156 / 0.0156 | 0.0155 / 0.0155 | unchanged |

TTFT is reported per completed request because at this load the default 300 s `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` retires requests on both sides before they are served, and unsent slots are recorded as zero.

Swept across five hit-rate tiers, varying segment length so the analytic ceiling runs 0.50 to 0.85 while the longest prompt stays at ~131K:

| tier | ceiling | wall clock baseline -> L2-Only | ratio | output tok/s | ratio | p99 TTFT | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H50 | 0.500 | 2h08m -> 41m | 3.12x | 0.38 -> 0.62 | 1.63x | 583 -> 279 | 2.09x |
| H67 | 0.667 | 3h09m -> 1h01m | 3.10x | 0.52 -> 0.91 | 1.75x | 553 -> 288 | 1.92x |
| H75 | 0.751 | 4h09m -> 1h25m | 2.93x | 0.61 -> 1.18 | 1.93x | 569 -> 295 | 1.92x |
| H80 | 0.801 | 5h15m -> 1h50m | 2.86x | 0.62 -> 1.15 | 1.85x | 542 -> 293 | 1.85x |
| H85 | 0.836 | 6h42m -> 2h35m | 2.59x | 0.68 -> 1.20 | 1.76x | 551 -> 355 | 1.55x |

All ten cells `exit=0`. TPOT and ITL are unchanged in every tier: the gain is in admission and TTFT, not in per-token decoding.

items.title: Fix disaggregated prefill cache leak after abort
items.body:
## Motivation

An aborted disaggregated prefill request can lose scheduler ownership when an overlapped middle or final chunk result arrives after AbortReq or bootstrap failure. The result path currently drops aborted middle chunks and does not check final chunks before caching and enqueueing them.

For hybrid Mamba models this leaves one request allocation unaccounted for: one full prefill chunk plus the request Mamba state and overlap buffers. The observed production invariant failure was a 16,384-token full-KV deficit and three missing Mamba states.

## Modifications

- Treat abort as terminal before optimistic-bootstrap retry.
- Retire aborted final results and abandoned middle results through one idempotent cleanup helper.
- Release metadata, HiCache request state, KV pages, and Mamba state without inserting the aborted request into radix cache.
- Defer cleanup while a later overlapped chunk is still running.
- Ignore delayed results when bootstrap-failure cleanup already released the request.
- Stream the terminal abort exactly once from the result path that owns cleanup.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output behavior changes for successful requests.

- 9 focused CPU tests passed, including delayed middle result, delayed final result, already-cleaned bootstrap failure, and unified-memory move-gate coverage.
- All file-scoped pre-commit hooks passed.

GPU reproduction on the original GLM-5.3-Flash B300 deployment is still pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The new checks only run for completed disaggregated-prefill results; no model-forward path changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (not needed for this lifecycle bug fix).

items.title: [PP] Batch independent chunks for small-chunk disaggregated prefill
items.body:
## Motivation

> **Scope correction:** This draft improves the case where each request is capped at a 2K chunk but the aggregate model-forward budget is increased to approximately 32K. It does **not** improve a model forward whose aggregate batch is fixed at 2K, so it is not a solution to the fixed-small-batch PP bubble problem. The corrected fixed-2K launch/control-overhead work is proposed separately in [#36248](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36248); the measurements below should be read only as an independent-chunk aggregation experiment.

In PP disaggregated prefill, `chunked_prefill_size` currently serves two different purposes: the per-request chunk boundary and the aggregate token budget of the entire forward batch. With `chunked_prefill_size=2048`, this limits every PP prefill forward to approximately 2K tokens even when many independent requests are waiting, so increasing client concurrency cannot recover GPU utilization and pipeline efficiency.

This PR separates those two limits for an opt-in PP disaggregated-prefill path: each request remains capped by `chunked_prefill_size`, while the batch can aggregate independent chunks up to `max_prefill_tokens`. For the evaluated 2K configuration, one forward can therefore combine up to approximately 16 independent chunks instead of launching one approximately 2K-token forward at a time.

## Modifications

This PR is organized as five dependency commits:

1. Add a per-request chunk limit to `PrefillAdder` and use `max_prefill_tokens` as the aggregate budget, allowing multiple independent middle chunks in one PP prefill batch.
2. Track, cache, transfer, and requeue all batched middle chunks without losing their committed ChunkCache progress.
3. Apply the same per-request chunk limit to the `ignore_eos` admission path so it cannot consume the aggregate budget as one request.
4. Let requeued middle chunks reuse the request-pool slots they already own when the pool is saturated.
5. Prioritize those slot-owning continuations whenever slotless requests would exhaust the remaining request slots before all continuations are visited, preventing both full-pool and partial-capacity head-of-line blocking.

The first item is the throughput mechanism. Items 2-5 are correctness and liveness requirements introduced by batching multiple independent middle chunks; they are not unrelated scheduler fixes. The new path is guarded by `SGLANG_PP_BATCH_INDEPENDENT_CHUNKS` and currently requires PP disaggregated prefill, `max_prefill_tokens > chunked_prefill_size`, overlap scheduling disabled, and ChunkCache (`--disable-radix-cache`). The default path is unchanged.

The patch intentionally excludes one-page tail merging, pure-middle-chunk PP output skipping, and 2K prefill BCG because their controlled peak contributions were small, inconsistent, or negative.

## Accuracy Tests

Matched GSM8K A/B used the same Qwen3.5 NVFP4 model, 4-GPU TP1 PP4 prefill, 4-GPU TP4 decode, and 2K per-request chunks. The protocol was 200 questions, five-shot chat, 128 threads, `temperature=0.6`, `top_p=0.95`, and `top_k=20`.

| Arm | Independent chunks | Aggregate budget | GSM8K score | Correct |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | off | 2,048 | 0.980 | 196/200 |
| After | on | 33,792 | 0.995 | 199/200 |

Both runs completed 200/200 requests without errors, and their captured request payloads were byte-identical. Since the protocol uses stochastic sampling without a per-request seed, this is an accuracy non-regression result rather than an accuracy-improvement claim.

Scheduler correctness tests: **6/6 passed**. `git diff --check`, seven-file `py_compile`, and lint also passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Setup

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-V2` |
| Precision | NVFP4 weights, FP8 KV cache |
| Prefill topology | 4 x GB300, TP1 PP4 |
| Decode topology | 4 x GB300, TP4 PP1 |
| Serving | Dynamo disaggregated prefill/decode with Mooncake transfer |
| Workload | random data, ISL=8192, OSL=1, request rate=inf |
| Concurrency | 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 |
| Requests per point | 10 x concurrency |
| Page size | 64 |
| Prefill settings | overlap disabled, radix cache disabled, dynamic chunking disabled, CUDA graph disabled, max running requests=128 |
| Before 2K | `chunked_prefill_size=2048`, aggregate budget=2048 |
| After 2K | `chunked_prefill_size=2048`, `max_prefill_tokens=33792`, aggregate FlashInfer dispatch budget=33792 |
| 32K reference | `chunked_prefill_size=max_prefill_tokens=32768` |
| Metric | aggregate input tokens/s |

The controlled five-point performance run used the final no-tail/no-output-skip ablation source with runtime semantics equivalent to this PR. After diagnosing the C256 result, a same-configuration C128/C256 follow-up changed only the partial-capacity queue-ordering rule and source identity. The five commits were then cleaned and transplanted onto current upstream `main`; the final main-based branch reran the targeted correctness and formatting tests but did not repeat the GB300 sweep. Every benchmark point completed all requests with exact 8192/1 lengths and zero non-empty errors.

### Baseline chunk-size sweep

| Chunk size | C16 | C32 | C64 | C128 | C256 | Peak concurrency | Peak input tok/s |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2K | **30,507** | 30,318 | 30,093 | 29,873 | 29,690 | **C16** | **30,507** |
| 4K | 58,392 | **58,652** | 58,442 | 57,617 | 57,027 | **C32** | **58,652** |
| 8K | 113,512 | **114,642** | 114,614 | 113,200 | 113,069 | **C32** | **114,642** |
| 16K | 116,059 | 166,216 | 167,231 | **168,354** | 167,057 | **C128** | **168,354** |
| 32K | 88,803 | 139,336 | 176,180 | **177,586** | 177,273 | **C128** | **177,586** |

The original 2K peak reached only 17.18% of the 32K peak. Raising client concurrency from 16 to 256 reduced 2K throughput by 2.68%, confirming that the aggregate forward shape, rather than request supply, was the limiting factor.

### 2K before and after

| Concurrency | Original 2K | Batched 2K | Matched-concurrency speedup | 32K reference | Batched 2K / 32K |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 30,507 | 60,417 | 1.98x | 88,803 | 68.04% |
| 32 | 30,318 | 84,924 | 2.80x | 139,336 | 60.95% |
| 64 | 30,093 | 135,633 | 4.51x | 176,180 | 76.99% |
| 128 | 29,873 | 170,652 | 5.71x | **177,586** | 96.10% |
| 256 | 29,690 | **171,489** | **5.78x** | 177,273 | **96.74%** |

Peak-to-peak, the final core path improves 2K throughput from 30,507 tok/s at C16 to 171,489 tok/s at C256: **5.621x / +462.12%**. It reaches **96.74%** of the matched-concurrency 32K reference while preserving a 2K per-request chunk boundary. C128 also remains non-regressed at 170,652 tok/s, and C256 is 0.49% above C128 rather than falling 20.53% below it.

The C256 follow-up directly isolates the partial-capacity queue-ordering change:

| C256 metric | Before partial-capacity fix | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Input throughput | 133,843 tok/s | **171,489 tok/s** | **+28.13%** |
| Benchmark duration | 156.69 s | **122.29 s** | **-21.95%** |
| Mean TTFT | 15,196.7 ms | **11,718.7 ms** | **-22.89%** |
| P99 TTFT | 19,355.3 ms | **13,827.6 ms** | **-28.56%** |
| PP0 full 33,792-token batches | 472 / 897 (52.62%) | **614 / 640 (95.94%)** | **+43.32 pp** |
| Mean PP0 new tokens per batch | 23,445.5 | **32,860.6** | **+40.16%** |

Both C256 runs completed 2560/2560 requests with exact 8192/1 lengths and zero non-empty errors. Before the fix, a large waiting queue still produced repeated 2K multiples because a few newly available request slots were consumed by slotless requests before the scan reached slot-owning continuations. After the fix, the full-batch ratio rises to 95.94%, which explains the throughput recovery without changing the 2K per-request cap or any kernel.

An earlier batching-only prototype already reached 52,246 / 92,368 / 143,483 tok/s at C16/C32/C64, or 1.71x / 3.05x / 4.77x over the original 2K baseline, before request-slot saturation stopped C128. This isolates independent-chunk aggregation as the primary throughput mechanism; the slot reuse and queue-ordering commits make the new mechanism complete at C128/C256 rather than accelerating an individual GPU forward.

### Excluded micro-optimizations

These increments were measured in the controlled sweep before the final partial-capacity queue follow-up and are not combined with the new C256 result.

| Incremental change | C16 | C32 | C64 | C128 | C256 | Peak effect |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| One-page tail merge over core | +8.45% | -4.29% | -2.84% | +0.43% | +6.10% | +0.43% |
| Pure-middle output skip over tail | +3.58% | +8.10% | +2.33% | +0.72% | -2.01% | +0.72% |
| 2K prefill BCG | approximately -4% | approximately -4% | approximately -4% | not continued | not continued | negative |

Tail merging plus output skipping increased peak throughput from 168,421 to 170,363 tok/s, only +1.15% in one run, while showing inconsistent effects across concurrency. They are intentionally left out of this PR so the upstream patch contains only the dominant batching mechanism and its required correctness/liveness support.

- Use the logical HiSparse capacity when admitting transferred prompts on decode workers.
- Use the same capacity when calculating the generation budget.
- Preserve physical-capacity behavior for other configurations.
- Add regression tests for long prompts and `max_new_tokens` initialization.

items.title: Fix clearing transferred Mamba state in disaggregated decode
items.body:
## Motivation

A successful disaggregated transfer initializes the destination Mamba cache slot, but the request can remain marked for clearing. The next initialization step may therefore discard the transferred recurrent state before decoding.

## Modifications

- Clear `mamba_needs_clear` after committing a real transfer containing Mamba state.
- Preserve existing behavior for fake transfers and transfers without Mamba state.

## Accuracy Tests

- Verified exact monolithic/disaggregated output parity for BF16, W4A16, and W4A4 configurations.
- `ruff` checks passed.
- `black --check` passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable; the change adds one state update after transfer completion.

items.title: [Scheduler] Restore disaggregated decode overlap with resource leases
items.body:
## Motivation

PR #31687 fixed a disaggregated decode use-after-free race by waiting on the WAR fence immediately after every launch. The fence is correct, but it also serializes result processing, queue maintenance, and request admission behind the GPU forward and creates a scheduler bubble.

Moving the fence back later recovers performance but is unsafe: finished requests can release and reuse request-pool rows or KV pages while the in-flight forward still reads them.

## Modifications

- Add a per-forward resource lease over request-pool rows, guarded by row generations.
- Wait on the existing read-done marker only before shared mapping mutations.
- Quarantine finished request slots and KV pages until the protecting forward epoch completes.
- Preserve the immediate global fence for unaudited session, cache, offload, multimodal, staging, and control paths.
- Add focused coverage for lease lifecycle, generation validation, result processing, retraction, admission overlap, and fail-closed fallbacks.

This PR is a new standalone change based on current `main`; it does not reuse or update #31270. The lease path is opt-in with `SGLANG_ENABLE_DISAGG_DECODE_RESOURCE_LEASE=1`; the default keeps the immediate global WAR fence.

## Accuracy Tests

- 28 focused resource-lease tests pass after rebasing onto current `main`.
- Full-repository pre-commit passes.
- The same build also passed six DSV4 WAR regression tests and two parameterized subtests.
- 65,626 benchmark requests completed with zero errors.

items.title: Fix waiting-timeout cleanup for disaggregated requests
items.body:
## Motivation

`SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT` could remove timed-out waiting requests without cleaning up resources owned by disaggregated requests.

In disaggregated decode, waiting requests may already own KV cache. In disaggregated prefill, waiting requests may own metadata buffer state and finalized KV senders. The timeout cleanup was also only reached from the normal scheduler path, while disaggregated decode and prefill use separate scheduling loops.

## Modifications

- Run waiting-timeout cleanup from both disaggregated scheduler loops:
  - `get_next_disagg_decode_batch_to_run`
  - `get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run`
- Reuse waiting-queue abort cleanup for timeout-driven aborts.
- Release disaggregated decode KV cache for timed-out waiting requests.
- Abort finalized disaggregated prefill senders before releasing metadata buffers.
- Mark timed-out requests as `FINISH_ABORT` before releasing KV cache, so session-backed cache cleanup treats them as aborted instead of successful completions.
- Add focused unit tests for cleanup behavior and reachability from the disaggregated scheduler loops.

## Direct Proof

### Timeout cleanup was unreachable in disaggregated scheduler loops

Before this change, `_abort_on_waiting_timeout()` only ran from the normal scheduler path. Disaggregated decode and prefill use separate scheduling loops:

- `get_next_disagg_decode_batch_to_run()`
- `get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run()`

So requests sitting in those waiting queues could exceed `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT` without running timeout cleanup.

This PR calls `_abort_on_waiting_timeout()` directly from both disaggregated loops. The tests `test_disagg_decode_scheduler_runs_waiting_timeout_cleanup` and `test_disagg_prefill_scheduler_runs_waiting_timeout_cleanup` prove those loops now invoke the cleanup path.

### Timed-out cache-owning requests must be marked aborted before KV release

`release_kv_cache()` eventually calls `tree_cache.cache_finished_req(...)`. For streaming sessions, `StreamingSession.try_cache_finished_req()` distinguishes abort cleanup from successful completion by checking:

```python
isinstance(req.finished_reason, FINISH_ABORT)
```

So if a timed-out waiting request owns KV/session state and releases KV before setting `FINISH_ABORT`, the session path can treat the request like a successful finish.

This PR sets `req.finished_reason = FINISH_ABORT(...)` before `_release_waiting_queue_abort_resources(req)` can call `release_kv_cache(...)`. The test `test_waiting_timeout_releases_disagg_decode_kv_cache` asserts this ordering directly inside the mocked `release_kv_cache` call.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This does not change model forward computation or expected model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This only runs when waiting-queue timeout cleanup is enabled and a request exceeds `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT`.

items.title: [PD] Pin disaggregated decode KV pages with refcounts
items.body:
## Summary

This change fixes a KV-page lifetime race in PD disaggregation decode.

Related issue: #24527

## Root Cause

In PD disaggregation, decode preallocates destination KV pages before the prefill-side KV transfer has fully finished. Those pages are then visible to two different lifetimes at the same time:

- the decode request lifetime, which can abort and release its preallocated KV slots early
- the prefill transfer writer lifetime, which may still be in flight and still writing into the same destination pages

Before this change, the allocator only tracked request ownership. If decode aborted first, the request-level release path could return those pages to the free list immediately even though the prefill-side writer had not actually finished yet. A later request could then reuse the same pages, and the stale writer from the old request could overwrite KV data that now belonged to a new request.

That race shows up as cross-request KV corruption: the model output looks wrong, but the underlying issue is page reuse happening before the transfer writer is done with those pages.

## Test Plan

- run allocator-level checks to verify retain/free semantics and ensure pages are not returned to the free list until all references are released
- run PD fault-injection reproduction where decode aborts while prefill transfer is still delayed/in flight, and confirm the old writer can no longer race with page reuse
- run normal PD success-path traffic and confirm the extra writer reference is released after successful transfer completion
- run long-context, multi-request stress traffic to confirm there is no refcount underflow, allocator leak, or idle self-check regression while delayed writer releases are pending
- compare baseline and patched serving performance under the same PD workload to measure the incremental retain/free overhead

items.title: [codex] Pin disaggregated decode KV pages with refcounts
items.body:
## Summary

This change fixes a disaggregated decode KV-page lifetime bug by pinning preallocated decode KV pages with allocator reference counts until the transfer writer is known to be finished.

## Root Cause

In PD disaggregation, decode preallocates destination KV slots before the prefill-side transfer finishes. If decode aborts the request early, the request-level release path can recycle those slots while the prefill writer is still in flight, allowing stale writes to land on pages that have already been reassigned.

## What Changed

- add reference counts to token and paged KV allocators
- mark pages as allocated on alloc and only return them to the free list when the refcount reaches zero
- retain decode preallocated KV pages after transfer metadata is sent so the writer owns an extra reference
- release that writer reference when the transfer succeeds
- delay writer-reference release for aborted transfers to avoid reusing pages while an orphaned writer may still be in flight
- skip decode idle self-checks while delayed writer releases are pending so intentionally pinned pages are not treated as leaks

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator.py python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py`
- manual PD fault-injection validation in our test environment confirmed that an aborted decode request no longer allows its preallocated pages to be immediately reused while the transfer writer is still pending

## Impact

This change makes disaggregated decode page reuse robust against transfer abort races without changing the normal allocator interface for callers.

## Motivation

The current MoRI disaggregation path assumes a single `dst_kv_item_len` (int) applies to every layer on the destination. For architectures that expose different item sizes per layer (e.g., MLA models, or cases where the prefill and decode sides have non-uniform KV shapes), this causes address computation to use the wrong stride for all layers but the first, corrupting the KV cache transfer.

## Modifications

All changes are confined to `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mori/conn.py`.

- `KVArgsRegisterInfo`: replace `dst_kv_item_len: int` with `dst_kv_item_lens: List[int]` (per-layer). A `dst_kv_item_len` property is retained for backward compatibility (returns the first element).
- Wire format: the list is sent in `payload[11]` using msgpack; when absent or empty, the parser falls back to broadcasting the legacy scalar across all layers, so peers still running the old protocol remain compatible.
- `MoriKVManager._split_descs_and_lens()` (renamed): accepts `KVArgsRegisterInfo` and returns per-layer `src_/dst_k_item_lens` and `src_/dst_v_item_lens` alongside the descriptor lists.
- RDMA scheduling uses the per-layer lens when computing source and destination strides.

## Known overlap / caveat for reviewers

Open PR #22665 ("[PD] MORI-IO: Add state transfer, inline transfer model, and high-concurrency fixes") also extends `KVArgsRegisterInfo` and the `from_zmq` parser, introducing `dst_state_item_lens` / `dst_state_dim_per_tensor` at `payload[11]` / `payload[12]`. This PR uses `payload[11]` for `dst_kv_item_lens`. Both changes are orthogonal in intent (state transfer vs. per-layer KV item lens) but collide on the wire slot. If either lands first, the second should renumber its slot(s) during rebase.

items.title: [Bug] Preinitialize KV transfer metrics for non-disaggregated deployments
items.body:
## Summary
- preinitialize KV transfer metric series when the scheduler metrics collector is constructed
- keep `/metrics` stable in non-disaggregated deployments where no KV transfer ever occurs
- add a regression test that guards the preinitialization hook in `SchedulerMetricsCollector`

## Root Cause
The KV transfer metrics are implemented as labeled Prometheus gauges and histograms. In non-disaggregated deployments there is no KV transfer/bootstrap path, so the corresponding metric children are never created via `labels(...).set(...)` or `observe(...)`. Under Prometheus multiprocess mode that means the `/metrics` endpoint omits those series entirely, which looks like null/empty metrics instead of valid zero-valued ones.

## Fix
Pre-create the KV transfer-related metric children for the current scheduler label set during `SchedulerMetricsCollector` initialization. Queue gauges are initialized to `0`, and histograms are initialized by creating their labeled children without recording a fake observation.

## Testing
- `python -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py test/registered/metrics/test_kv_transfer_metrics.py`
- `python test/registered/metrics/test_kv_transfer_metrics.py`

Fixes #21167

items.title: [sgl-model-gateway] Add EPD (Encode-Prefill-Decode) Disaggregated Routing Support
items.body:
## Motivation

Following the recent kernel-level support for EPD disaggregation in SGLang (see [PR #12263](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/12263)), this PR implements EPD (Encode-Prefill-Decode) disaggregated routing for sgl-router, enabling efficient multimodal LLM inference by separating the encode, prefill, and decode stages across specialized workers. This extends the existing PD (Prefill-Decode) mode to support vision-language models like Qwen2.5-VL.

Key Problem Addressed:
- Multimodal models need to process images/videos separately from text
- Traditional single-worker or PD-mode serving underutilizes resources for vision-language workloads
- PD mode lacks the encode stage required for efficient multimodal input processing

Architecture Pattern:

~~~
User Request (with images/video)
↓
Encode Worker (HTTP) → Processes images/video, sends embeddings
↓
Prefill Worker (gRPC) → Receives embeddings, computes KV cache
↓
Decode Worker (gRPC) → Generates output tokens using KV cache
↓
Response
~~~

## Modifications

**Core Infrastructure**

Triple Dispatch Pattern:
- Extended the pipeline framework to support three-stage dispatch (EPD) alongside existing single dispatch (Regular) and dual dispatch (PD)
- New WorkerSelectionMode::EncodePrefillDecode for selecting HTTP encode + gRPC prefill/decode workers
- New ExecutionMode::TripleDispatch for coordinating encode HTTP call with prefill/decode gRPC streams

HTTP Client Module:
- Created dedicated HTTP client for encode worker REST API (src/http_client/)
- EncodeHttpClient with configurable timeout and connection pooling
- EncodeRequest/EncodeResponse types for multimodal encoding requests

Worker Types:
- WorkerType::Encode: HTTP-based encode workers with optional bootstrap port
- WorkerType::Prefill: gRPC-based prefill workers with ZMQ embedding receiver
- WorkerType::Decode: gRPC-based decode workers

**Pipeline Stages**

WorkerSelectionStage:
- select_epd_triple() method selects encode (HTTP) + prefill (gRPC) + decode (gRPC) workers
- Separate routing policies per worker type (encode_policy, prefill_policy, decode_policy)
- Falls back gracefully if encode workers unavailable

RequestBuildingStage:
- Injects EPD metadata (request IDs, worker IDs, prefill host info)
- Sets need_wait_for_image flag for prefill scheduler synchronization
- Clears multimodal inputs from prefill request (already sent to encode)

RequestExecutionStage:
- execute_triple_dispatch() coordinates three-stage execution:
	a. Extract multimodal items from chat messages
	b. Call encode worker HTTP /encode endpoint
	c. Parallel gRPC dispatch to prefill and decode workers
	d. Handle streaming responses
- Automatic fallback to PD dispatch for text-only requests
- Circuit breaker tracking for all three worker types

## **Configuration**

New routing mode in RouterConfig:

~~~rust
RoutingMode::EncodePrefillDecode {
	encode_urls: Vec<(String, Option<u16>)>,
	prefill_urls: Vec<(String, Option<u16>)>,
	decode_urls: Vec<String>,
	encode_policy: Option<PolicyConfig>,
	prefill_policy: Option<PolicyConfig>,
	decode_policy: Option<PolicyConfig>,
}
~~~

Python bindings:

- `--epd-disaggregation` flag to enable EPD mode
- `--encode` for encode worker URLs
- `--encode-policy` for encode-specific routing policy
- `--encode-selector` for Kubernetes service discovery

**Fallback Behavior**

- Text-only requests automatically fall back to PD mode (no multimodal encoding needed)
- Missing encode workers trigger warning and fallback to PD
- Graceful degradation ensures service continuity

## **Metrics**

Prometheus metrics exposed for monitoring:
- Worker selection metrics per stage (encode/prefill/decode)
- Request latency histograms for triple dispatch
- Circuit breaker state per worker type
- Load tracking for all three worker pools

## Implementation Details

Architecture

~~~
src/
├── http_client/
│   ├── mod.rs              # HTTP client module exports
│   └── encode.rs           # Encode worker HTTP client
├── routers/
│   ├── grpc/
│   │   ├── epd_router.rs   # GrpcEPDRouter implementation
│   │   └── common/
│   │       └── stages/
│   │           ├── worker_selection.rs  # EPD worker selection
│   │           ├── client_acquisition.rs # Triple client handling
│   │           └── request_execution.rs  # Triple dispatch logic
│   └── factory.rs          # Router creation with EPD support
├── config/
│   └── types.rs            # EncodePrefillDecode routing mode
└── context.rs              # Triple worker/client selection types
~~~

Communication Protocols

Encode Worker HTTP API:

~~~
POST /encode
{
"mm_items": ["image_url1", "base64_data"],
"req_id": "uuid",
"prefill_host": "prefill-worker-host",
"embedding_port": 9000
}

Response:
{
"embedding_size": 1024,
"embedding_len": 1024,
"embedding_dim": 4096
}
~~~

Embedding Transfer:
- Encode worker sends embeddings directly to prefill via ZMQ
- Router coordinates by passing prefill host/port to encode worker
- Prefill scheduler waits for embeddings before processing (need_wait_for_image flag)

Execution Flow

1. HTTP request arrives at router with multimodal content
2. Router extracts multimodal items (images/videos) from chat messages
3. WorkerSelectionStage selects encode (HTTP), prefill (gRPC), decode (gRPC) workers
4. Router calls encode worker HTTP /encode endpoint with multimodal items
5. Encode worker processes images/video, sends embeddings to prefill via ZMQ
6. Router dispatches gRPC requests to prefill and decode workers in parallel
7. Prefill receives embeddings, computes KV cache, streams to decode
8. Decode generates output tokens, streams response back
9. ResponseProcessingStage merges and returns final response

## Usage

Enable EPD Support

~~~
# Launch encode worker (HTTP)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
--model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct \
--encoder-only \
--port 30300

# Launch prefill worker (gRPC)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
--model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct \
--grpc-mode \
--disaggregation-mode prefill \
--language-only \
--encoder-urls http://127.0.0.1:30300 \
--port 30301

# Launch decode worker (gRPC)
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
--model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct \
--grpc-mode \
--disaggregation-mode decode \
--port 30302

# Launch EPD router
python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \
--host 127.0.0.1 \
--port 30000 \
--epd-disaggregation \
--model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct \
--encode http://127.0.0.1:30300 \
--prefill grpc://127.0.0.1:30301 9000 \
--decode grpc://127.0.0.1:30302 \
--policy cache_aware

# Multi-Worker Deployment

python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \
--epd-disaggregation \
--encode http://encode1:8080 \
--encode http://encode2:8080 \
--encode http://encode3:8080 \
--prefill grpc://prefill1:9000 9000 \
--decode grpc://decode1:8001 \
--decode grpc://decode2:8002 \
--encode-policy round_robin \
--prefill-policy cache_aware \
--decode-policy power_of_two

# Kubernetes Service Discovery

python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \
--epd-disaggregation \
--encode-selector tier=encode \
--prefill-selector tier=prefill \
--decode-selector tier=decode
~~~

## Testing

E2E Tests (py_test/e2e_http/test_epd_router.py):
- Real GPU tests with Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct
- MMLU benchmark (text-only, tests PD fallback)
- MMMU benchmark (multimodal, tests full EPD)
- GenAI-bench performance testing
- Multi-worker cluster benchmarking (6 encode + 1 prefill + 1 decode)
- Integration with sglang.bench_serving

Test Configuration

Dataset: MMMU (Math subset, 32 prompts)
Hardware: 3x GPUs (1 encode, 1 prefill, 1 decode)

Cluster Setup:

Prefill Worker → GPU 1, Port 30002 (gRPC)
Decode Worker → GPU 2, Port 30003 (gRPC)
EPD Router → Port 30000

## Future Work

Dynamic Encoder Pool

The current implementation uses static encoder-to-prefill mappings configured at router startup. A planned enhancement is to implement a Dynamic Encoder Pool architecture:

Design Goals:
- Prefill workers dynamically establish connections with encode workers based on real-time workload and encoder availability
- Support elastic scaling of encoder instances without router restart
- Optimize resource utilization for multimodal workloads

Architecture:

~~~
                      ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │         Encoder Pool                │
                      │  ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌───────┐  │
                      │  │Encode-1 │ │Encode-2 │ │  ...  │  │
                      │  └────┬────┘ └────┬────┘ └───┬───┘  │
                      │       │           │          │      │
                      │       └───────────┼──────────┘      │
                      │                   │ (ZMQ)           │
                      └───────────────────┼─────────────────┘
                                          ▼
                                ┌─────────────────┐
                                │ Prefill Worker  │ ← Dynamic connection
                                │ (Pool Manager)  │   based on workload
                                └────────┬────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                                ┌─────────────────┐
                                │ Decode Worker   │
                                └─────────────────┘
~~~

Rationale:
- Multimodal data (images/videos) can be processed in parallel across multiple encoders
- Typical production deployments use many encoder instances with fewer prefill/decode instances (e.g., 6:1:1 ratio)
- Dynamic pooling allows prefill workers to:
- Load-balance across available encoders
- Handle encoder failures gracefully
- Scale encoder capacity independently

Planned Capabilities:
- Encoder health monitoring and automatic failover
- Workload-aware encoder selection (e.g., route large images to less-loaded encoders)
- Support for heterogeneous encoder configurations (different GPU types, batch sizes)
- Auto-discovery of new encoder instances via service mesh integration
